title: Self-Hosting Foundation and Compiler Subset Contract
purpose: Define the first BASIC# subset allowed for future compiler-writing work while Ruby remains the bootstrap compiler and reference authority.
compiler_subset_allows: file-shaped source text handled by the existing Ruby bootstrap during this build
deterministic token records for future reader work
plain data contracts expressed as JSON specifications

self_hosting_sequence.goal: Record the rejected v0.1.43 package, then freeze this foundation contract and validation gate.
Build a BASIC# tokenizer/reader contract and fixture set before implementation.
Implement tokenizer/reader pieces with Ruby as referee and compare deterministic records.
Parse a small approved compiler subset into deterministic records under Ruby Parser referee.
Emit BSharp IR from small compiler subset records under Ruby Parser plus SemanticResolver referee.
Lock golden IR parity for the small compiler subset.
Lock plain-English error records for invalid small compiler subset examples.
Expand the small compiler subset across larger scene/block fixtures under Ruby referee.
Emit BSBC from BASIC# compiler code and require byte-for-byte parity before replacing Ruby.

acceptance_rules: All existing Profiles 1-7 validation remains mandatory.
Ruby remains the bootstrap and reference oracle in v0.1.63.
The self-hosting contract tool must pass before package acceptance.
No future build may call BASIC# self-hosted until the BASIC# compiler reproduces approved outputs under locked validation.
The small compiler subset parser tool must pass before package acceptance.
The small compiler subset IR emitter tool must pass before package acceptance.
The small compiler subset IR golden parity harness must pass before any future bytecode-emission self-hosting lane can claim progress.
The small compiler subset plain-English error contract must pass before invalid subset errors can be considered stable.
The small compiler subset scene/block expansion harness must pass before wider self-hosting subset claims can advance.
The small compiler subset symbol table contract must pass before wider self-hosting subset claims can advance.
The small compiler subset BSBC emitter must pass before wider self-hosting bytecode claims can advance.
The small compiler subset BSBC golden parity harness must pass before wider self-hosting bytecode claims can advance.
The self-hosting fixture corpus tool must pass before wider self-hosting subset claims can advance.
The small compiler subset runtime smoke lane must run under Ruby referee control and must not change production runtime behaviour.
The bootstrap boundary audit must pass before v0.1.63 may claim Self-Hosting Milestone 1 readiness.
The README Current Release Truth Gate must pass so the public GitHub README matches the active build.
The Self-Hosting Milestone 1 gate must pass before v0.1.63 may be accepted.
v0.1.63 may claim only BSharp Compiler Subset 0 Self-Hosting Milestone 1 under Ruby referee control, not full self-hosting.
